summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Galena Health through org- and project-level rate limits, quota controls, and RBAC for multi-tenant setup. Customer cares about per-project quotas, burst behavior, audit trails, and KMS integration for keys. Agreed to run a 1-week PoC benchmark and exchange security docs.
topics: Per-key rate limits and burst capacity
transcript:
[00:00] Nina (AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, I see Sophie, David, Priya — thanks for carving out time. Marcus is on from our SE team, he'll run through the console and the rate-limit configs. we have 45 minutes so we'll go through the demo and leave time for q's.

[00:18] Sophie (CTO): Thanks Nina. We're evaluating vendors for inference endpoints. key things for us are multi-tenant isolation, per-tenant quotas, and making sure keys can't be abused. we want to avoid noisy neighbors.

[00:35] Marcus (SE): Totally. Today I'll show two main flows: org-level controls (global quotas, org-wide rate limiting), and project / api-key level controls for teams. We'll demo the Redwood Console and then the API side for enforcement.

[00:48] David (Infra): quick question — do you do hard caps or leaky-bucket style? our load is spiky during business hours.

[00:55] Marcus (SE): Good call. We support both. You can set hard caps per-project that will reject requests past the limit, or token-bucket/leaky-bucket with burst allowances. We also support burst pools for dedicated customers so you can absorb short spikes without failing. There's also automatic fallback routing to lower-cost model variants if capacity is constrained.

[01:12] Priya (Security): for audit — we need per-request logs with API key, project, org, and model used. retention for 12 months. Also KMS for key material.

[01:21] Nina (AE): we have SOC 2 + ISO summaries — I'll share those. Marcus, can you show where audit logs are surfaced?

[01:27] Marcus (SE): yep. switching to the console. (screen share) here is the org dashboard — top-left you see org-wide quotas, tokens consumed, active projects. I'll click into Projects -> 'Galena-Dev' project.

[01:42] Marcus (SE): In the project settings you can configure: per-minute and per-day token quotas, request QPS, and per-route quotas (so you can throttle completions differently from embeddings). Example: embeddings jobs have higher per-request cost so you can set a lower tokens/day cap.

[02:05] Sophie (CTO): can we do different quotas for different teams but under same billing org? we have product and research teams.

[02:13] Marcus (SE): yes — that's exactly the org/project model. You create projects under an org and issue project API keys. Billing can be aggregated at org level or split across projects depending on billing settings. Keys are scoped to project permission sets.

[02:25] David (Infra): how is key rotation handled? we have short-lived keys via our vault.

[02:30] Marcus (SE): We support rotating keys via the dashboard and API; you can also integrate with customer KMS/HSM for keys in Private deployment. For hosted we store encrypted key material and you can force rotation; for Private we can integrate with your KMS so Redwood never holds plaintext.

[02:45] Priya (Security): And SSO? RBAC granularity? we need admin vs billing vs dev roles.

[02:50] Marcus (SE): SAML/SSO + SCIM provisioning supported. RBAC roles include Org Admin, Billing Admin, Project Admin, Developer, Read-only. You can tie roles to project keys; the console shows effective permissions when you generate keys.

[03:05] Sophie (CTO): what's enforcement on the API side? i.e. if someone hits a key above QPS, what's the response?

[03:12] Marcus (SE): by default you'll get 429 with a structured error body that includes current quota, reset time, and we optionally return a retry-after header. We also offer graceful degraded responses — e.g., if you allow fallback, requests can be routed to a smaller model or to cached responses for prefix hits.

[03:32] David (Infra): any risk of misattribution? say a key is leaked — can we emergency disable a project key without affecting the rest of the org?

[03:39] Marcus (SE): yes you can revoke a project key immediately, and you can flag suspicious activity. We have per-key kill switch in console and API. Also audit logs show the IP, user-agent, and model used so you can investigate.

[03:52] Nina (AE): i'll drop links in the follow-up: security whitepaper, rate-limits doc, and the sample PoC plan.

[04:00] Marcus (SE): demoing the API now — simple header X-Redwood-Key with project key. Example curl: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <project_key>' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"..."}' . Response will include usage tokens in the response metadata.

[04:22] Sophie (CTO): you mentioned per-route quotas. can we set a daily cap for the /embeddings route only? we run nightly bulk embeddings.

[04:30] Marcus (SE): yes you can set route caps and enforce schedule windows. For bulk jobs we recommend using a separate project key for batch workloads so it doesn't eat into interactive quotas. You can also set time-based limits — e.g., embeddings allowed only during off-peak windows.

[04:50] David (Infra): what about shared pools if we're on Dedicated? we want predictable latency but don't want to overprovision for spikes.

[04:58] Marcus (SE): Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools with SLA-backed latency. You can configure a burst pool that draws from spare capacity; that has throttling rules and cost controls. For cost-sensitive teams, Redwood Optimize suggests quantization and batching settings per workload.

[05:15] Priya (Security): encryption at rest and in transit — confirm KMS + HSM options for Private deployments?

[05:21] Marcus (SE): Affirmative. Hosted: customer data encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys via KMS integration (optional). Private: can be deployed in your VPC and use your HSM; Redwood control plane can be run in a private mode if needed. We'll share the integration guide.

[05:35] Sophie (CTO): any guardrails for abuse detection? like rate-limit anomalies or sudden uptick detection?

[05:42] Marcus (SE): We have anomaly detection alerts in Console tied to usage thresholds. You can create alerting rules (email, Slack, webhooks) when a project exceeds expected QPS or token burn. Also automated rules can throttle or suspend a key if suspicious behavior matches patterns.

[06:00] Nina (AE): let's run a quick scenario — assume product team has 3 daily services using the same project key and research team runs nightly batch embeddings. how would you recommend setup?

[06:12] Marcus (SE): I'd recommend separate projects: 'product' with interactive quotas and per-route throttles, and 'research-batch' with a higher daily token cap and restricted time window. Issue a separate project key for CI and rotate frequently. Set org-level guardrails to stop any single project from consuming >80% of org tokens.

[06:40] Sophie (CTO): ok that seems good. how long to stand up the PoC? we want to validate latency and cost for our typical prompts.

[06:48] Nina (AE): we usually do a 1-week PoC. Marcus will provide a test spec and we'll run traffic from your infra or ours, whichever you prefer.

[06:56] Marcus (SE): i'll draft a benchmark with seq len distributions, QPS targets, and token budgets. we'll measure p95/p99 latency and tokens per request. We'll also include a validation for org/project rate limits and revocation tests.

[07:10] Priya (Security): can you sign an NDA quick? we need to share a subset of prompts that are sensitive.

[07:16] Nina (AE): yes we can. i'll kick off legal to send a mutual NDA.

[07:22] Sophie (CTO): any concerns about regional data residency? we process EU patient attributes.

[07:28] Marcus (SE): Redwood supports region pins; Hosted can pin to EU region, and Private gives full regional control. Audit logs include region info. We'll include data residency notes in the security pack.

[07:40] David (Infra): final - pricing structure for org/project keys? do you charge per-key or per-org consumption?

[07:46] Nina (AE): pricing is usage-based at org level, but project keys help you partition consumption for internal chargeback. For Dedicated/Private it's contract-based with reserved capacity. I'll share a pricing sheet with examples for tiered org/project quotas.

[07:58] Marcus (SE): quick note on implementation - in code it's just setting the Authorization header per request. On infra side, we recommend instrumenting responses that include token-usage so your telemetry can correlate cost to request type.

[08:12] Sophie (CTO): wrap up — this was helpful. next steps?

[08:16] Nina (AE): action items: i) send security docs and pricing, ii) Marcus will send PoC benchmark plan, iii) Galena to provide security baseline & sample prompts under NDA, iv) schedule pilot kickoff for week of 12/28. I'll also share the console recording.

[08:34] Priya (Security): thanks, please include SOC2 attestation and KMS integration docs in the send.

[08:40] Nina (AE): will do. thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email.

[08:45] (call ended)

Notes: Shared artifacts referenced during call: redwood-rate-limits-deck.pdf, redwood-security-summary.pdf, galena-poc-spec-template.xlsx. Some transcription artifacts: 'KV cash' misheard for 'KV cache' in a couple places; occasional speaker mislabels.
